fatal_blocker: The 2011 final-cover investigation used ten narrow backhoe test pits along the perimeter landfill-gas header to inspect geosynthetic integrity. It did not publish measured final-cover soil thicknesses or define two broad measured depth polygons. Phases I and II have one repeated cover profile, while the Old Barney White Landfill has a different construction history and no coordinate-tied final measured thickness grid.
key_evidence: The 2011 investigation excavated ten test pits through final-cover soil along the north, west, south and a small east perimeter portion above the landfill-gas header.
Typical test pits were approximately 50 to 60 feet long and 4 feet wide.
The report concluded the geosynthetic cover was intact, but did not provide a table of measured soil-cover thickness values.

The post-closure plan describes Phases I and II with one repeated profile: 12 inches vegetative topsoil/cover soil, geotextile, 12-inch drainage layer, geonet composite, geomembrane and 6-inch low-permeability soil.
The Old Barney White Landfill was closed and later upgraded under a different construction history, so it is not a matched near-surface comparison zone.
Periodic reviews support long-term maintenance and current cover integrity, but do not supply the missing measured depth pair.
next_action: Continue the approved search for a full-scale vegetated closure containing two broad coordinate-tied final measured as-built depth zones under the same near-surface construction.
